analogs.covers: Almost everything: a lifelong pair holding a huge territory, sky-dance courtship, grab-and-drop kills, war on rival raptors

headline: A pair of golden eagles holding a huge territory, grabbing prey and dropping it from the sky.

setting.label: Huge territories over open country, canyons and coasts
setting.note: Mated pairs claim an entire POI. All Hatzegopteryx migrate yearly to a shared courtship ground where they are uniquely tolerant of each other.

playsLike: You are a Large daytime flier (air sprint 1,100). Once you have paired for life at the courtship grounds, you and your mate claim an entire POI and chase out every other Hatzegopteryx and aerial species. You hunt what you can carry: clamp it, fly high, drop it. Solo you hunt up to Medium tier and 2+ up to Large, plus any hatchling or juvenile even when it is protected. Quetzalcoatlus is a rival you must kill or drive out.

why.text: Pairs for life and defends a large territory together. Golden eagle pairs hold one territory for life (official inspiration).
Courtship is a display of spectacular aerial dives, like the golden eagle's undulating display flights.
Prefers prey it can pick up, clamps it and drops it from a height, the way eagles drop tortoises onto rocks.
Must chase all aerial species out of its territory and kill or evict Quetzalcoatlus. Eagles attack rival raptors on sight.
May hunt any hatchling or juvenile even if an adult protects it, just as eagles snatch lambs and kids from their mothers' sides.

notLike: A golden eagle is small next to most of its targets; Hatzegopteryx is a Large-tier giant (3,100 combat weight) that also walks and fights on the ground.
twist: Marsh harriers and barn owls are official inspirations too: aerial courtship displays and a hunter's eye for movement.
